subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` gain a core skill-context injection contract, and what selection, redaction, prompt-layer, audit, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source-level capability gap is clear, but the requested feature crosses ACP session state, external harness trust, local skill content exposure, and Codex-native skill behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design the ACP contract first
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers specify explicit/default/auto selection, redaction and audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to explicit skill ids
options.body: Approve only an explicit `skills` selector for ACP spawns and defer automatic/default injection until observability and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Keep ACP harnesses isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skills and point users to harness-native skills, MCP, or plugin workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Design the ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this open while maintainers specify explicit/default/auto selection, redaction and audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the ACP runtime/control-plane surface that the requested contract would extend.
